title: 8-Ball Pool: One Drag, Two Modules, and a Full Rules Engine Behind Every Shot
subtitle: A rebuild of classic 8-ball pool as a physics-archetype duel against an AI: drag distance folds into 18 power levels, all-stopped settlement keeps the rules trustworthy, fouls hand over ball-in-hand, and AI aim error keeps the match alive. Fully playable demo at the end.

breakdown.title: Rule Skeleton
bullets: Standard 8-ball: 16 balls (cue + 1-15), solids 1-7 vs stripes 9-15, the 8 goes last
The first ball pocketed after the break assigns both players' groups
Three foul states — cue ball pocketed, no ball contacted, opponent's ball hit first — hand the opponent ball-in-hand
Clear your group then legally sink the 8 to win; sinking it early or on a foul loses on the spot

breakdown.title: Behavior Loop
bullets: Press near the cue ball → drag to set direction and power (drag distance maps to 0-18) → release to shoot
Frame-by-frame physics: ball-ball collisions, cushion bounces, pocket detection, settled only after everything stops
Settlement judges fouls, group assignment, and pocket ownership — keep shooting or hand over; the AI answers in 1-1.5s
A legal 8-ball finish pops the result screen; PLAY AGAIN rematches instantly

breakdown.title: Implementation Notes
bullets: 8-ball/pool-model carries physics and rules in one module: ball states, collision/pocket detection, foul and winner logic, plus the AI shot
__OV.Games.EightBallPool.Game is the scene-private renderer: PIXI draws table, balls and cue, translating pointer events into shot.aim/drag/release
A real race had to be fixed: LogicGraph runs async, so resetting the aiming flag must defer to a macrotask or a real drag can never fire a shot
common-ui wires pause/help buttons; the boot → menu → gameplay ⇄ paused → result state machine is declared in the blueprint

demo.note: Hit Play to break. Press near the cue ball, drag to aim, release to shoot — the farther you drag, the harder the hit. Clear your group, then sink the 8; the AI takes its turns automatically.
